page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6t.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance belonging to the Enhanced family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware resource provisioning excludes integrated local storage, meaning that block storage requirements must be met through external network-attached cloud disks. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which necessitates explicit configuration of network routing or Elastic IP addresses for external internet traffic.

The 1:4 balance between processing cores and memory provides balanced hardware capacity for non-bursting, continuous operations. Because dedicated CPU resources avoid noisy-neighbor contention, the instance offers consistent compute performance. It suits enterprise workloads such as relational database hosting, intermediate enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, container orchestration worker nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and medium-to-large web application deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6t.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Enhanced instance family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 hardware. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz and provides 128.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The instance lacks onboard local disk storage and includes no integrated graphics processors, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Because of its dedicated core allocation and balanced resource profile, it functions efficiently for workloads requiring stable computational throughput and moderate memory density, including production application servers, relational database management systems, mid-tier enterprise platforms, and automated continuous integration environments.
